newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: MTV plans Asian expansion with new Indian channel.
newsitem.headline: MTV plans Asian expansion with new Indian channel.

text.p: MTV Networks Asia, a unit of Viacom Inc., said Monday it would launch an Indian channel and relocate the production base for its Mandarin channel from Singapore to Taipei by the end of October.

Linda Stiles, a spokeswoman for MTV Networks Asia, said Singapore would remain the company's regional headquarters, and its three Asian channels would be post-produced and broadcast from the city-state.
She told Reuters that MTV India would give Indian viewers access to new shows produced domestically and in Singapore, and a higher rotation of Indian music videos, interviews and news features.
The launch of the Indian channel would allow MTV Asia, the company's existing regional channel, to concentrate more on its Southeast Asian markets, Stiles said.
"The other big market we address is Indonesia," she said, adding, however, that she did not expect the launch of an Indonesian MTV channel "for quite some time."
The relocation of MTV Mandarin's production base to Taipei will bring the channel closer to the region's Mandarin-speaking and music markets.
Stiles said 10 to 15 employees would be added to the Taipei office, including the relocation of on-air personalities and other staff from Singapore.

She said the company had laid off eight production staff at its Singapore office, but would be hiring up to 10 more people over the next month in a range of areas, including advertising and sales, to support MTV India and MTV Asia.
